headline: Bangladesh observes World Teachers' Day today, honouring 101 educators
summary: World Teachers' Day is celebrated globally on October 5 to recognize the invaluable contributions of teachers in shaping societies and fostering intellectual growth. In Bangladesh, 101 distinguished educators are being honored for their dedication.
details: World Teachers' Day is being observed today, October 5, to honor the profound contributions of educators worldwide. Teachers are considered the architects of a nation, guiding individuals in intellectual development and moral values.
The day has been celebrated globally since 1995, following its establishment by UNESCO. It serves as an occasion to acknowledge their vital role in society and uphold their dignity.

Bangladesh, like many other countries, observes this day annually, with government initiatives now supporting its celebration. This year, 101 meritorious teachers are being felicitated for their exceptional service.

The decision to celebrate World Teachers' Day on October 5 was adopted at UNESCO's 26th General Conference in Paris in 1993. The first observance took place in 1994, with widespread international adoption beginning in 1995.

headline_marked: [[Man beaten to death]] in Pabna on suspicion of theft; police investigate
headline: Man beaten to death in Pabna on suspicion of theft; police investigate
summary: A rickshaw puller, identified as Sumon, 30, was found severely injured and later died at Pabna General Hospital. Family members reported multiple injury marks on his body.
details: A 30-year-old rickshaw puller, Sumon, was allegedly beaten to death in Pabna's Gachpara area on suspicion of theft. He succumbed to his injuries while undergoing treatment at Pabna General Hospital on Sunday afternoon, October 4.

Family members stated that an unidentified rickshaw puller left Sumon, severely injured, near a shop in front of their house around noon on Sunday. After being rescued and taken home, his condition worsened, leading to his transfer to the hospital where doctors declared him dead.

According to family members, Sumon had multiple injury marks on his body. The Officer-in-Charge (OC) of Pabna Sadar Police Station, Tariqul Islam, stated that preliminary findings suggest Sumon was physically assaulted sometime on Sunday due to his suspected involvement in a theft at a house in Bilbhaduri area a few days prior.
Police have identified suspected individuals involved in the incident and are conducting operations to apprehend them. No case has been filed yet regarding the death.
